entries.title: Preserve Gauntlet as a positional territorial card game
entries.summary: The rebuild preserves the defining hook: player-built Territory line, tactical advance and retreat, card commitment, capture, and running the Gauntlet.

entries.title: Reject an arbitrary round limit as the pacing solution
entries.summary: Game length should be solved through gameplay pressure and lasting progress, not an external round cap in the ordinary game.

entries.title: Reject breach and damage markers as unnecessary complexity
entries.summary: Territory progress should use occupation, counterattack, and capture rather than a separate breached/damaged state.

entries.title: Movement is a voluntary choice, not a movement roll
entries.summary: On the normal Movement step, choose to advance, hold, or withdraw one position. Movement itself is not resolved by opposed dice.

entries.title: Use separate hand commitments and temporary Battle Hands
entries.summary: Each side may commit up to one card from the normal hand, then draws a temporary Battle Hand and may choose up to one eligible card from it.

entries.title: Hand commitments are permanent; Battle Hand cards recycle
entries.summary: After battle, used cards from the normal hand go to the Graveyard while chosen and unchosen Battle Hand cards normally go to the Discard Pile.

entries.title: One normal Action Opportunity may be used before or after movement
entries.summary: A player normally has one Action Opportunity each turn and chooses whether to use it before movement or, if unused, after movement.

entries.title: A battle ends the movement sequence
entries.summary: Beginning a battle ends the current movement and loses unused movement unless a specific effect permits movement afterward; the after-movement Action Opportunity remains.

entries.title: Occupation precedes capture and grants one counterattack turn
entries.summary: An attacker who wins occupies enemy Territory. If still there at the start of the attacker’s next turn, it is captured; the defender has the intervening turn to retake it.

entries.title: Asset limit equals controlled Territories
entries.summary: A player’s Asset limit equals Territories controlled; occupied-but-uncaptured Territories do not count, and excess Assets are discarded when control is lost.

entries.title: Do not adopt the simulated minimum-two Asset floor
entries.summary: A minimum-two Asset floor was explored as a softer anti-snowball variant, but the released rule retains the cleaner exact Territory-controlled limit without a floor.

entries.title: Use advantage and disadvantage instead of large modifier ladders
entries.summary: Ordinary probability manipulation uses advantage/disadvantage and restrained modifiers; the old ±2 through ±5 modifier ladder is not the design baseline.

entries.title: Tie rerolls continue the same battle state
entries.summary: When an unresolved tie is rerolled, previously used cards and ongoing battle effects remain active; the battle does not reset.

entries.title: Deck construction remains at least 30 cards and at most 60 value
entries.summary: Playable Decks contain at least 30 cards, no more than 60 total value, and exactly three different Territories with no more than one Arena.

entries.title: The final victory requires winning the battle beyond the Gauntlet
entries.summary: Reaching the far end does not itself win. The defender makes a Last Stand beyond the Gauntlet and the attacker must win that battle.
